hero.body:
A Fort Pierce woman was arrested for using counterfeit currency to pay for her meal in St. Lucie County, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office. On August 22, deputies responded to a reported theft involving a food delivery in which the customer used two counterfeit $50 bills as payment for the $83.90 order.

 On Monday, deputies learned that the individual who used the counterfeit money was staying at a residence on Miramar Avenue in Fort Pierce. Upon arrival, they quickly identified Adrianna Marie Sheppard, 19, as the person who provided the fake money.

 Sheppard was arrested and charged with fraud utter bank bill, note, check or draft, as well as possession of counterfeited bank bill, note, check or draft and larceny.

hero.body:
A Fort Pierce man faces a manslaughter charge after a 34-year-old man died following a BB gun shooting on August 22, 2026. Fort Pierce Police officers responded to the 2900 block of Avenue G following reports of a gunshot victim.

Upon arrival, officers located the 34-year-old male suffering from an injury. The victim was transported to Lawnwood Hospital, where he later died.

The initial investigation revealed that a group of males had been shooting a BB gun at trees when the suspect, Jabari Cowart, 36, asked to use the BB gun. During the interaction, Cowart reportedly pointed the BB gun in the victim's direction and fired. Shortly thereafter, the victim collapsed.

Cowart was charged with manslaughter and taken to the St. Lucie County Jail. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation.

hero.angle: Lead with the update confirming MCSO's Air One helicopter crew spotted the Palm City garage fire and directed crews in time to save the home; detail the destroyed garage, motorhome and Jeep, and note the State Fire Marshal has been called in as cause remains under investigation.

hero.body:
A Martin County Sheriff's Office helicopter crew spotted a large fire late Sunday night and alerted firefighters in time to prevent flames from spreading to a nearby home on Southwest Martin Highway in Palm City. The MCSO Air One pilot and tactical flight observer were on patrol around 10:30 p.m. when they noticed flames coming from a detached garage and immediately alerted deputies and Martin County Fire Rescue.

 Firefighters arrived to find the roughly 1,600-square-foot structure engulfed in flames with its roof already gone. The fire was threatening the main home on the property. Crews were able to contain the blaze before it reached the house. The homeowners were not home at the time.

 Firefighters found a Class C motorhome and a Jeep inside the structure. The garage and both vehicles were completely destroyed.

 The State Fire Marshal was notified. The cause of the fire remains under investigation. The sheriff's office said the helicopter crew's discovery allowed emergency crews to reach the property in time to keep the flames from spreading to the home.

hero.body:
A Martin County Sheriff's Office helicopter crew spotted a detached garage fire along Southwest Martin Highway in Palm City late Sunday night and alerted firefighters in time to save the main home on the property. The MCSO Air One pilot and tactical flight observer were on patrol around 10:30 p.m. when they noticed flames coming from the garage and immediately alerted deputies and Martin County Fire Rescue, according to the sheriff's office. The roughly 1,600-square-foot garage, a Class C motorhome inside it, and a Jeep were completely destroyed.

Firefighters arrived to find the structure engulfed in flames with its roof already gone. The sheriff's office said the fire was threatening the main home on the property. Crews were able to contain the blaze before it reached the house.

The homeowners were not home at the time, according to MCSO. Firefighters found the motorhome and Jeep inside the structure, both of which were destroyed along with the garage.

MCSO praised the Air One crew and responding deputies and firefighters, saying the helicopter crew's discovery allowed emergency crews to reach the property in time to keep the flames from spreading to the home. Martin County Fire Rescue said the State Fire Marshal was notified. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office says that on August 14, it is believed that Racqueal Annalessa Martin went to Loves Truck Stop in Fort Pierce and got a ride from a truck driver to another Loves Truck Stop located in Memphis, Tennessee. However, she has been reported missing since, and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is now seeking the public's assistance in finding Martin.

She was last seen wearing a black and green shirt with get money written on it, black and white shorts, and black flip-flops while carrying a dark-colored bag. Martin is a black female standing at 5-foot-6, weighing approximately 140 pounds with hazel colored hair, and brown eyes. Anyone with information is encouraged to call 911 or contact Detective Corporal Bogner at 772-462-3230.

hero.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado with peak winds of 75 mph touched down in Port St. Lucie before becoming a waterspout as it moved over the St. Lucie River Sunday evening. According to Will Ulrich, a warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service, the tornado touched down at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitchen Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, near the Tarpon Bay Club. It traveled a little more than two miles over 14 to 15 minutes. The tornado then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout that meandered slowly over the water for five to seven minutes before moving back onshore near the Bay St. Lucie community at about 6:20 p.m.

Ulrich said the strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community before the circulation continued west into Port St. Lucie's Southbend area, where it caused a discontinuous damage path of some trees down, along with some homes that had fences blown over and some pool screen enclosures that were damaged or destroyed. Allison Rogers, who lives off of Southbend Boulevard across from Jessica Clinton Park, had her fence blown down during the storm. Another woman who lives across the street from where the tornado started had parts of her roof ripped off. Carol Cadotte voiced her frustration with receiving the alert for the tornado well after it passed her house. Cadotte said her phones went off 20 minutes later.

Ulrich said this tornado was unique in multiple ways. It was not raining when it touched down; the heavy rain came afterward, which he said is typical of how landspouts form. Unlike most tornadoes, it did not spin out of a rotating supercell thunderstorm; it formed along the leading edge of one. Ulrich said the problem with landspouts is that the circulations are not particularly strong, such that the National Weather Service can very easily see it on radar. The weather service knows there is a weak circulation, but Ulrich said they see weak circulations all the time, so that does not necessarily always lead to a tornado.

The National Weather Service said it is also aware of damage reported in Jensen Beach. Based on preliminary information from Martin County Emergency Management, storm spotter calls and videos submitted to local media, forecasters said a brief landspout or tornado likely developed near the Treasure Coast Square Mall. The weather service said the possible tornado lofted a small amount of debris and caused minor damage. In Jupiter, a large tree fell across the road near Donald Ross Road and Central Boulevard Sunday night. Jupiter police responded and blocked the area to prevent drivers from hitting the tree.

cards.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening with peak winds of 75 mph. The tornado began at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitchen Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, near the Tarpon Bay Club. It traveled a little more than two miles over 14 to 15 minutes.

The tornado then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout. Will Ulrich, a warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said the waterspout remained over the St. Lucie River for five to seven minutes, traveling from north to south before moving back onshore near the Bay St. Lucie community at about 6:20 p.m.

The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community before the circulation continued west into Port St. Lucie's Southbend area. The weather service said the tornado caused damage including trees down, fences blown over, and some pool screen enclosures that were damaged or destroyed. No homes were damaged, and there were no injuries.

cards.teaser: An EF0 tornado with maximum estimated wind gusts between 65 and 75 mph touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening and moved over the St. Lucie River as a waterspout.

cards.body:
Aron Christiansen spent Monday morning pulling debris out of his pool after already retrieving furniture from the bottom. Video from a neighbor's camera captured the moment his patio broke apart during the storm. Half of the patio is now out on the curb, set to be salvaged for recycling. Christiansen said he looked out the windows Sunday night and saw a bunch of debris flying. He thought it was birds at first, but looked closer and saw debris. He had about 10 seconds before it hit the house.

Janelle Pierre-Louis said she was surprised by the amount of damage to her backyard foliage after dealing with damage at the front of her house first. Her front door caved in because the door is kind of old. Dirt came through the cracks.

Around the corner, Mitch Brewer had debris piled out front, most of it from a shed he had tied down. Marlene Torres was in a good mood Sunday night before returning home to find the storm had moved through her neighborhood. She had just come back from Jensen Beach celebrating her birthday. Her home was not damaged, but she needed an electrician to fix her meter.
cards.headline: Port St. Lucie residents clean up debris after EF0 tornado tears through neighborhood
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie residents spent Monday cleaning up after Sunday night's storm tore through the area, leaving behind damaged structures, debris-filled pools and downed foliage.

cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District responded to a residential fire on Sunday in the 400 block of East Erie Drive in Fort Pierce following reports of a residential structure fire. When fire district crews arrived at the scene, they quickly attacked the fire, containing the fire to the area of origin, which prevented the fire from spreading to nearby mobile homes.

The cause of the fire is being investigated by the Florida State Fire Marshals. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and the Fort Pierce Police Department also responded to the incident.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a woman for using counterfeit currency to pay for her meal in St. Lucie County. On August 22, deputies responded to a reported theft involving a food delivery in which the customer used two counterfeit $50 bills as payment for the $83.90 order.

On Monday, deputies learned that the individual who used the counterfeit money was staying at a residence on Miramar Avenue in Fort Pierce. Upon arrival, they quickly identified Adrianna Marie Sheppard, 19, as the person who provided the fake money. She was promptly arrested and charged with fraud utter bank bill, note, check or draft, as well as possession of counterfeited bank bill, note, check or draft and larceny.

Drivers who stay longer than two hours will receive a $50 citation, which increases to $100 for repeat offenses. The initiative, which began in July, aims to increase parking turnover, improve traffic flow, and make it easier for visitors to find available spaces, according to city officials.

Owner of Notions Potions, Beryl Muise, said the two-hour parking limit has benefited her business. She has seen her customers be able to find a parking spot and come into the store, and then get back into their car and be able to leave. While there are two free parking garages nearby, some businesses have expressed concerns. One restaurant, which declined to comment on camera, said two hours is not long enough for their lunch rush, especially with limited parking in front of the establishment.

The two-hour parking limits are enforced Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Muise said weekends are less congested, benefiting retail and restaurants. The city of Fort Pierce has not yet responded to inquiries about the number of citations issued.

hero.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado with peak winds of 75 mph touched down in Port St. Lucie before becoming a waterspout as it moved over the St. Lucie River Sunday evening. According to Will Ulrich, a warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service, the tornado touched down at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitchen Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, near the Tarpon Bay Club. It traveled a little more than two miles over 14 to 15 minutes. The tornado then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout that meandered slowly over the water for five to seven minutes before moving back onshore near the Bay St. Lucie community at about 6:20 p.m.

Ulrich said the strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community before the circulation continued west into Port St. Lucie's Southbend area, where it caused a discontinuous damage path of some trees down, along with some homes that had fences blown over and some pool screen enclosures that were damaged or destroyed. Allison Rogers, who lives off of Southbend Boulevard across from Jessica Clinton Park, had her fence blown down during the storm. Another woman who lives across the street from where the tornado started had parts of her roof ripped off. Carol Cadotte voiced her frustration with receiving the alert for the tornado well after it passed her house. Cadotte said her phones went off 20 minutes later.

Ulrich said this tornado was unique in multiple ways. It was not raining when it touched down; the heavy rain came afterward, which he said is typical of how landspouts form. Unlike most tornadoes, it did not spin out of a rotating supercell thunderstorm; it formed along the leading edge of one. Ulrich said the problem with landspouts is that the circulations are not particularly strong, such that the National Weather Service can very easily see it on radar. The weather service knows there is a weak circulation, but Ulrich said they see weak circulations all the time, so that does not necessarily always lead to a tornado.

The National Weather Service said it is also aware of damage reported in Jensen Beach. Based on preliminary information from Martin County Emergency Management, storm spotter calls and videos submitted to local media, forecasters said a brief landspout or tornado likely developed near the Treasure Coast Square Mall. The weather service said the possible tornado lofted a small amount of debris and caused minor damage. In Jupiter, a large tree fell across the road near Donald Ross Road and Central Boulevard Sunday night. Jupiter police responded and blocked the area to prevent drivers from hitting the tree.
hero.headline: NWS confirms EF0 tornado with 75 mph winds touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday
